title: Protocol for aquaphotomics monitoring of water molecular structure in leaves of resurrection plants during desiccation and recovery
protocol: Prepare plant materials according to established protocols.
Grow three biological replicates of Haberlea rhodopensis and Deinostigma eberhardtii in a growth chamber at specified conditions for at least two months after the last subculture.
Start dehydration procedure with well-developed and rooted plants that are at least two months old.
Remove three plantlets from culture vessels and leave them to dry in open air under controlled conditions.
Allow Haberlea rhodopensis plantlets to reach full dry state within 24 hours.
Dehydrate Deinostigma eberhardtii plantlets for up to 168 hours until water content reaches approximately 10%.
Store fully desiccated Haberlea rhodopensis under controlled conditions for 10 days before rehydration.
Rehydrate dried plantlets by placing them on moist cotton beds for 24 hours.
Separate the leaves of the prepared plant material with a surgical knife.
Place the separated leaves on the gold reflector cell.
Perform spectral acquisition in transflectance mode.
Set spectral range from 1100 to 2500 nm using WinISI II software version 1.50.
Configure resolution step at 2 nm and average each spectrum with 32 scans.
Measure three spectra for different leaves of each plant.
Acquire spectra at the following time points: 0, 1, 2, 3, 6, and 24 hours after starting desiccation for H. rhodopensis.
Acquire spectra at the following time points: 0, 1, 3, 6, 24, 48, 72, 120, and 168 hours after beginning desiccation for D. eberhardtii.
Acquire spectra at 1, 2, 3, 6, 24, and 48 hours after starting rehydration for H. rhodopensis.
Acquire spectra at 1, 3, 6, and 24 hours after undertaking rehydration for D. eberhardtii.
Perform extended multiplicative scatter correction (EMSC) to eliminate scattering effects arising from different thickness and surface properties of leaves.
Calculate difference spectra by subtracting the averaged spectrum of each plant’s fresh leaves from the corresponding averaged spectra of leaves at various time points of dehydration and rehydration.
Perform Principal component analysis (PCA) with leave one sample out cross validation as an exploratory analysis of spectral variation during desiccation and rehydration processes.
Calculate second derivative spectra using Norris gap second derivative on EMSC treated spectra to reveal the presence of hidden and overlapped peaks of the water species.
Based on the peaks discovered in the previous step, calculate ratios of water species absorbing at the found water absorbance bands.
Calculate the relative absorbance of water species for each time point.
Divide As by the sum of mean absorbances for all water species at that time point to find Arel,s.
Plot the calculated relative absorbances on a stacked column chart.
Each column in the chart corresponds to a certain time point during dehydration and rehydration.
